Food guide · Pizza · New York

The Pizza Styles of New York State

How many pizza styles does New York have?

The Local Legends Map counts 8 pizza styles born in New York: New York Slice (New York City), Coal-Oven Pie (New York City), Sicilian Square (Brooklyn), Grandma Pie (Long Island), Bar Pie (Staten Island), Buffalo-Style (Buffalo & Western NY), Upside-Down (Utica) and Cold Cheese Slice (Oneonta). Plus 4 local cousins that locals won't call pizza: Utica Tomato Pie, North Country Pizza Roll, Open-Face Calzone and Schenectady Tomato Pie. Places are voted by locals on Local Legends Map.

Ask for "a slice" in Brooklyn, Buffalo and Utica and you'll get three different things. Here's what each place means by pizza, and where locals get it.

The pies

1
New York City

New York Slice

Crust
Thin and hand-stretched, crisp underneath but soft enough to fold
Sauce
A light tomato sauce
Cheese
Low-moisture mozzarella

The big, wide slice sold over the counter from a round pie. It's the default pizza of New York City and the one the rest of the country copies.

Order like a local: One plain slice, folded lengthwise, eaten standing up.

Where locals send youJoe's Pizza Greenwich VillageMap
The Pizza page →
2
New York City

Coal-Oven Pie

Crust
Thin, blistered and charred at the edges from a coal fire
Sauce
Bright tomato
Cheese
Fresh mozzarella in patches

The old-school New York pie, baked fast in a coal-fired oven. Most coal-oven pizzerias sell whole pies only, no slices.

Order like a local: A whole plain pie for the table. Don't ask for a slice.

Where locals send youLombardi's Little Italy, ManhattanMap
More from New York City →
3
Brooklyn

Sicilian Square

Crust
Thick, airy and spongy, baked in a rectangular pan
Sauce
Plenty of it. At L&B it goes on top of the cheese
Cheese
Mozzarella, under the sauce at L&B

New York's thick square slice. The dough rises in the pan, so it comes out light inside with a crisp, fried bottom.

Order like a local: A square or two, then spumoni for dessert at L&B.

Where locals send youL&B Spumoni Gardens Gravesend, BrooklynMap
More from New York City →
4
Long Island

Grandma Pie

Crust
Thin, pressed into an oiled square pan
Sauce
Crushed tomato spooned on after the cheese
Cheese
Mozzarella first, then the tomato

The thin square that Long Island made famous. It started as the pizza home cooks made in a sheet pan, then the pizzerias put it on the menu.

Order like a local: A square pie with garlic and basil. Grab a corner piece.

Where locals send youUmberto's New Hyde Park, Long IslandMap
More from Long Island →
5
Staten Island

Bar Pie

Crust
Cracker-thin and crisp all the way to the edge
Sauce
A thin layer
Cheese
Mozzarella out to the rim

A small, personal-size pie with almost no crust edge, built to go with a beer. Staten Island's taverns are known for it.

Order like a local: One pie per person, with a beer.

6
Buffalo & Western NY

Buffalo-Style Pizza

Crust
Thick and pillowy with a crisp bottom
Sauce
Sweet and well seasoned
Cheese
A heavy blanket of mozzarella, edge to edge

A thick, pillowy crust, sweet tomato sauce and a heavy blanket of mozzarella, topped with cup-and-char pepperoni that curls into little cups and crisps at the edges in the oven.

Order like a local: A large pepperoni with cup-and-char, and a dozen wings on the side. In Buffalo, that's one order.

Where locals send youBocce Club Pizza BuffaloMapLa Nova BuffaloMap
The Buffalo-Style Pizza page →
7
Utica

Upside-Down Pizza

Sauce
On top, over the cheese and toppings
Cheese
Underneath the sauce, with grated Romano on top

Utica's other pie, and this one comes out hot. The cheese and toppings go on the dough first, and the sauce goes on top with a finish of grated Romano. O'Scugnizzo Pizzeria has made it this way since 1914.

Order like a local: Order it at O'Scugnizzo and eat it hot.

Where locals send youO'Scugnizzo Pizzeria UticaMap
The Upside-Down Pizza page →
8
Oneonta

Cold Cheese Slice

Crust
A standard pizzeria slice
Sauce
Red sauce
Cheese
Melted mozzarella, then a heap of cold shredded mozzarella on top

Oneonta's late-night legend: a hot cheese slice buried under a big handful of cold, shredded mozzarella, added right before it's served. Tino's Pizza on Main Street made it famous in the 1980s, feeding bar-hopping students from SUNY Oneonta and Hartwick College. The story locals tell is that the cold cheese kept people from burning their mouths on slices fresh out of the oven. Ask for "a cold cheese" and you'll get one.

Order like a local: Ask for "a cold cheese" at Tino's, late at night, the way the college crowd does.

Where locals send youTino's Pizza OneontaMap
The Cold Cheese Slice page →

Pizza's cousins

Made from pizza dough, sold at pizzerias and bakeries, and locals will argue they're not pizza at all.

9
Utica

Utica Tomato Pie

Crust
Thick, focaccia-style, baked in a sheet pan
Sauce
Thick tomato sauce
Cheese
No mozzarella, ever. Grated Romano only

Utica's tomato pie isn't pizza, and locals will tell you so. A thick, spongy focaccia-style crust is baked in a sheet pan, topped with thick tomato sauce and dusted with grated Romano. There's no mozzarella, ever. It's cut into squares, sold by the sheet at bakeries, and eaten at room temperature or even cold.

Order like a local: A sheet from a bakery, eaten at room temperature or even cold.

The Tomato Pie page →
10
St. Lawrence Valley

North Country Pizza Roll

Crust
Pizza dough rolled up around the filling

The North Country's late-night tradition. The epicenter is Sergi's in Potsdam: generations of SUNY Potsdam, Clarkson and St. Lawrence students know the Sergi's Pizza Roll. In Canton, Josie's is the other name locals give you.

Order like a local: A Sergi's Pizza Roll in Potsdam, late at night.

Where locals send youSergi's Italian Restaurant PotsdamMapJosie's Little Pizzeria Bar and Lounge CantonMap
The Pizza Rolls page →
11
Corning & Elmira

Open-Face Calzone

Crust
Calzone dough, served open instead of folded shut

Order a calzone around Corning and it may come out open-face. Ask the locals which shops still make it that way.

Order like a local: Order a calzone and ask the locals which shops still make it open-face.

12
Schenectady

Schenectady Tomato Pie

Crust
Bread-like, from a coal-fired brick oven
Sauce
Tomato sauce
Cheese
Grated cheese

Schenectady's own take on tomato pie: a bread-like crust topped with tomato sauce and grated cheese. Perreca's Bakery, run by the same family for more than 100 years in Schenectady's Little Italy, bakes it in a coal-fired brick oven alongside its famous crusty Italian bread. It's a close cousin of Utica's tomato pie, and both cities will tell you theirs is the one.

Order like a local: Grab tomato pie and a loaf of the bread at Perreca's Bakery.

Where locals send youPerreca's Bakery SchenectadyMap

Good to know

Questions travelers ask

What is Buffalo-style pizza?

A thick, pillowy crust, sweet tomato sauce and a heavy blanket of mozzarella, topped with cup-and-char pepperoni that curls into little cups and crisps at the edges in the oven.

What's the difference between a grandma pie and a Sicilian slice?

Both are square. A Sicilian rises in the pan, so it's thick and airy. A grandma pie is thin, pressed into an oiled pan and topped with mozzarella first, then crushed tomato.

Is Utica tomato pie pizza?

Locals will tell you no. It's a thick, focaccia-style crust baked in a sheet pan with thick tomato sauce and grated Romano, no mozzarella, eaten at room temperature or cold.

What is a bar pie?

A small, cracker-thin pie with cheese out to the edge, made to go with a beer. Staten Island taverns are known for it.

Where can I try New York's pizza styles in one trip?

Follow The Pizza Trail: 8 stops from Little Italy, Manhattan to Buffalo. Downstate stops are walkable in a day. Upstate is a weekend.
